changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7546-chart-series-keys-declared.md`

- names `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` → `packages/plugin-charts/src/AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Every one of the six is read by `normalizeSeries` (`@object-ui/plugin-charts`, `normalizeChartSchema.ts:242-255`) and does real work in `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` — `label` names the legend entry, `variant === 'comparison'` selects the muted overlay, `opacity` / `dashArray` set stroke and fill, `stack` becomes Recharts' `stackId`, `yAxis` binds the secondary axis. Any consumer of the parse output — `objectui check` / `objectui validate` via `safeValidateSchema`, a JSON schema derived from the mirror, or any pipeline that keeps `parse()`'s result — lost them outright.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `785d3a731` (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1504 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2088 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36152465783)

### ① Derived judgments

**The mapping — covered, and stated.** At head the file draws a recharts XAxis at four sites: scatter's number XAxis (~2294), the combo ComposedChart (~2406, `xAxisCommonProps`), the plain cartesian branch (~2523, `xAxisCommonProps`) and horizontal-bar's number XAxis (~2507, which takes `yAxisSpecProps(primaryY)`); horizontal-bar's categories are a `type="category"` YAxis (~2511). `placeXAxis` reaches all of them: `top` / `bottom` via `xAxisCommonProps` (bar, `column` alias, line, area, combo) and the scatter XAxis; `left` / `right` via the horizontal-bar category YAxis (`xAxisDown`). Radar draws a PolarAngleAxis, and pie / donut / funnel / treemap / sankey draw no axis; each of those branches returns before either `ChartFootnote note={xPositionNote}` site, and the normalizer keeps `xAxis` for every family (`normalizeChartSchema.ts` ~483), so an authored `xAxis.position` there is SILENT. **Horizontal-bar reading — right, and stated in code (the `placeXAxis` docblock and the JSX comment at the category YAxis), docs row and changeset.** The branch already routes `xAxis.format` to the category YAxis's `tickFormatter` (`xTickFormatter`, ~2520) and the spec `yAxis` to the number XAxis (~2507), so "the `xAxis` object follows the categories" is the reading the existing routing implies; `left` / `right` place it, `top` / `bottom` are refused. Measured: `right` puts the category ticks on the right; `left` / none on the left with no note; `top` / `bottom` note + left.

**A valid side is never also noted.** `placeXAxis` returns `across` / `down` OR `refused`, never both; every valid-side pin asserts the note is null (top on 5 families, hbar right, 11 controls). Measured bar `top` + `title`: no note.

**One false comment (non-blocking, wording).** The diff at ~1677 says "`chartType` is the EFFECTIVE family, so a horizontal-bar that became a combo through its series draws, and is placed, as the vertical combo it now is." `comboBaseFamily('horizontal-bar')` returns `undefined` (`normalizeChartSchema.ts` ~600), so `effectiveChartFamily` never widens a horizontal-bar. Measured: `chartType: 'horizontal-bar'` with series `bar` + `line` and `position: 'top'` stays horizontal (category ticks left, `top` refused with the note). Behaviour is right; the comment describes a path that does not exist. Replacement for its last two sentences: "`chartType` is the EFFECTIVE family: a bar / line / area whose series disagree is placed as the vertical combo it became; `comboBaseFamily` never widens a horizontal-bar, so one with mixed series stays horizontal and keeps the `left` / `right` reading."

**"A loud refusal, not silence" — yes, in the file's own terms.** `ChartFootnote` is the existing partial-answer channel: `unsized-rows` (pie / funnel / treemap), `unplotted-points` (scatter) and `omitted-rows` (sankey) are each a p element with `role="note"`, `data-chart-note`, class `px-1 text-xs text-muted-foreground`, hard-coded English prose naming the key and the value, no console warning, rendered in the `mt-1 shrink-0` slot under the plot. The new note is the same element with the same classes and visible text; measured: "xAxis.position is left — this chart's x axis runs across it, so it sits at the top or the bottom. It is drawn at the bottom." (hbar: "…its x axis sits on the left or the right. It is drawn on the left."). It is visible text, not a data attribute alone. i18n: NONE of the three sibling notes is translated (the only translated refusal in the file is `SeriesArityRefusal`, a `ChartRefusal`, via `useSafeTranslate('chart.scatterOneMeasure')`); the new note matches its siblings in this channel. `joinNotes` keeps scatter's `unplotted-points` note alongside it and returns a lone note bare, so single-note charts keep their DOM.

**The docs `position` row — publishes a false first sentence, unscoped ⇒ FAIL.** The row now reads "The side of the chart the axis belongs to. On `xAxis` it is …". The first sentence is unscoped and so covers `yAxis`, where `position` is not honoured at head. Source: `hasDualAxis` is `yAxes.length` above 1 (~1607); the right YAxis renders only under `hasDualAxis` (~2532) and is always `orientation="right"` taking `yAxes[1]`; the primary YAxis carries no `orientation` (~2524). Measured at head: bar with a lone `yAxis: [{ field: 'revenue', position: 'right' }]` draws its only value axis on the LEFT (every value tick `orientation="left"`, 0 notes, bars drawn); `position: 'top'` on a y entry draws left, silent; two entries `[{ revenue, position: 'right' }, { cost, position: 'left' }]` draw the value ticks on the right only (the normalizer binds a `position: 'right'` first entry's series to the right axis, `normalizeChartSchema.ts:526`, and the second entry is the right-hand axis whatever it says). The `yAxes` prop JSDoc (AdvancedChartImpl.tsx ~322, "a second entry (or one with `position: 'right'`) turns on the secondary axis") is false for the lone-right case too. The PR body itself concedes the sentence "stays false for a lone right-hand y entry". Exact replacement for the row's Effect cell: "The side of the chart the axis belongs to. On `xAxis` it is one of the two sides that axis can run along: `top` or `bottom` on bar (`column`), line, area and `scatter` charts, whose x axis runs across the plot; `left` or `right` on a `horizontal-bar` chart, where `xAxis` configures the category axis running down the plot. On `yAxis` it is not yet honoured: a lone entry with `position: 'right'` draws on the left, `top` / `bottom` on a y entry are taken in silence, and with two entries the second is always the right-hand axis whatever either `position` says (objectui#NNNNN, the y-side twin of objectui#10587)." — where objectui#NNNNN is the card for dev finding 2, which the seat must file first (the dev report says "noted, not filed"; a row cannot cite a card that does not exist).
